gaps: California: the youth brochure, child labor pamphlet, hours charts and work permit forms B1-1 and B1-4 are English only on the sites we could read. The California Department of Education pages for the permit forms were behind a bot wall, so ask your school office whether other languages exist.
Georgia: we found only a Spanish sheet.
New York: no Vietnamese, Tagalog or traditional Chinese card, and no translated working papers form was found.
Illinois: nothing for Chinese, Korean, Vietnamese or Tagalog speakers, and the permit steps are English only.
The Social Security Administration pages could not be read, so no Social Security links are listed.
Parents who sign a permit form: no state page says whether the school provides an interpreter. Ask the school office before you go.
note: These are official translations. The English version is the official one. If a translation and your school or state seem to differ, ask your school work permit office or the agency phone number.
